newsitem.title: VATICAN: Pope resumes religious services in St Peter's.
newsitem.headline: Pope resumes religious services in St Peter's.

text.p: Pope John Paul took part on Sunday in his first public religious ceremony since he underwent surgery to remove his appendix earlier this month.
The 76-year-old Pontiff, dressed in gold, blue and white vestments, appeared in St Peter's Basilica to attend the first part of a long service in the Eastern Byzantine rite.
He sat on a throne to the side of the flower-bedecked main altar in Christendom's largest Church.
The Polish Pope, now in the 19th year of his pontificate, appeared to be in relatively good form but seemed at times tired as he read his homily in Italian and English.
He remained in the church for 70 minutes. He was later due to appear from his window overlooking St Peter's Square to deliver his regular noon blessing and address.
Pope John Paul is still recovering from an operation to remove his appendix on October 8. He is due to return to a limited schedule this week, resuming private audiences.
Sunday's service was held in Old Slavonic, English and other languages and includes liturgical rituals not normally used in the west.

The ceremony was held to mark the 350th anniversary of the Union of Uzhorod, which sealed the return of the Eastern Orthodox Ruthene Church to union with the Roman Catholic Church after the great east-west split of 1054. Uzhorod was then part of the kingdom of Hungary.
Members of the Ruthenian Catholic Church now have communites in parts of eastern Europe as well as in the United States and Australia.
